Welcome to Taunton School
A very warm welcome to the Taunton School website. Our purpose is to enable each child to embrace their individuality, explore their passions and develop into confident, well-rounded adults ready to make a positive impact on the world.
Our school rests on four key pillars: a culture of ambition, a mindset for life, a sense of belonging and a global community. Three key values are espoused by all students and staff: humility, engagement and kindness. Our community is aspirational yet unpretentious. We seek to develop quiet self-confidence in our pupils, with no hint of arrogance. We encourage all students to engage fully with the range of opportunities available to them and, above all, we ask them to look after one another.
Please enjoy browsing our website and do take the opportunity to come and visit us. We look forward to welcoming you.
James Johnson Headmaster
Your Taunton School Journey
Pre-Prep
Sixth Form
International
Nursery
At our Nursery, we are renowned for our excellence in Early Years Education for those aged 0-4 years.
We are a happy and thriving community where plenty of time is spent enjoying fresh air in our recently developed playground and allotment, reading books in our new woodland library, and sleeping in our recently refurbished baby rooms. It is here the foundations are laid for the start of your child’s journey into an exceptional education.
Pre-Prep
Our Pre-Prep, for children aged 4-7 years, offers a safe and vibrant environment where every child can feel secure and happy, with the freedom to explore.
We offer a warm, friendly, and nurturing environment where our specialist staff look after the needs of each individual child. We encourage children to be creative, curious, and confident.
Our motto is ‘Be Kind, Be Keen’.
Prep
Our Prep School is home to 330 boys and girls between 7 and 13 with a happy boarding community of around 50.
Dedicated staff, strong pastoral care and brilliant facilities sum up our Prep School. A place where we encourage and support students to explore their passions to Find their Exceptional.
Our ethos is centered around ‘The TPS Way’: we aim high and try our best, we are active learners and curious, we try new things & embrace challenges, and we are humble & we are kind. Most students progress through to Senior School, which starts in Year 9.
Senior
At Taunton Senior School, whilst we are proudly ambitious for all of our students, their wellbeing is at the heart of all we do.
We offer excellent facilities, outstanding pastoral care, and exceptional academic and co-curricular opportunities. We are a thriving and vibrant school offering an exceptional education every day. Many of our students progress to our Sixth Form, which starts in Year 12.
Sixth Form
Our exciting Sixth Form is the only school in the UK to offer four academic pathways at Year 12, playing to the strengths of every student. Students can study A-Level, International Baccalaureate, BTEC or the International Foundation Programme.
We aim to deliver a first-class Futures Programme, equipping our young adults with the skills they need for exceptional futures anywhere in the world. More than 96% of our students go on to university, including entry to Russell Group and Oxbridge.
Many of our alumni are enjoying exceptional careers in sports, acting, law, medicine, and finance amongst many other industries.
International
We have been welcoming international students for over 100 years and Taunton School is home to students of over 60 nationalities. We are one inclusive family, celebrating diversity and our global community.
We offer a unique structure which ensures a successful transition for international students into the British education system, allowing us to offer a tailor-made approach to learning in our inclusive, welcoming, and friendly school.
Our Strategic Pillars
At Taunton School we believe in creating an educational environment that celebrates the uniqueness of every child.
Our vision is to deliver the exceptional every day. By fostering a culture of ambition, cultivating a mindset for life, nurturing a sense of belonging and embracing our global community, we provide an extraordinary educational experience that prepares our pupils for exceptional futures.

We are proud to be investing in an extensive world-class campus development project, which is currently underway.
We want to continue to inspire our pupils, creating an environment that puts academic achievement, co-curricular opportunities, and pastoral care at its core.

We are incredibly proud of our school, the students, and the staff, so when this is recognised by external judges and organisations, it becomes an indication of our excellence.
Taunton School has been shortlisted and won several awards over recent years and received outstanding reviews from independent directories, like the Good Schools Guide.
Our excellent recent ISI inspection report is available to read in full.
We look forward to welcoming you
Join our Headmaster, James Johnson, and the Taunton School Team at an upcoming open event.
This is the best way for prospective families to experience Taunton School with the opportunity to meet members of staff, tour the state-of-the-art facilities and ask questions.
We offer in-person and virtual options to suit everyone’s needs including tailored events for pre-prep and nursery, military families, international families, sixth form as well whole school open mornings.
The events will give you the chance to experience life at Taunton School for yourself.

Each year, we are delighted to recognise and support pupils who have academic, musical, dramatic, artistic or sporting gifts with a scholarship award.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome Statement from James Johnson | Taunton School
pageCache.text:
A very warm welcome to the Taunton School website. Our purpose is to enable each child to embrace their individuality, explore their passions and develop into confident, well-rounded adults ready to make a positive impact on the world.
Our school rests on four key pillars: a culture of ambition, a mindset for life, a sense of belonging and a global community. Three key values are espoused by all students and staff: humility, engagement and kindness. Our community is aspirational yet unpretentious. We seek to develop quiet self-confidence in our pupils, with no hint of arrogance. We encourage all students to engage fully with the range of opportunities available to them and, above all, we ask them to look after one another.
It is an extremely exciting time to join Taunton School. We are in the midst of a hugely ambitious campus development plan to enhance the school’s already outstanding facilities. Following the completion of the new Dining Hall (2020), Sixth Form Centre and Library (2022), Green Heart of the campus (2023), transformational improvements to Pre-Prep play space and to our all-weather sporting facilities (2024) we are soon to embark on an defining project to bring Taunton School, Taunton School International and Taunton School International Middle School on to one campus, ensuring that we deliver our exceptionally diverse educational offerings together.
In both our unrivalled breadth of academic offerings (GCSE, A-Level, IB, BTEC, one-year GCSE programme, Pre-Foundation Year and International Foundation Year) and in the extraordinary co-curricular opportunities, we play to the strengths of every child. Our recent ISI inspection has confirmed this, recognising a significant strength in the co-curriculum where the ‘programme has been carefully crafted by the school’s leaders, who take into account pupil’s views and show a deep understanding of how to unearth the potential of each pupil.’
Please enjoy browsing our website and do take the opportunity to come and visit us. We look forward to welcoming you.
James Johnson Headmaster

pageCache.pageTitle: Post 18 Careers Options | Taunton School Sixth Form
pageCache.text:
Overseeing careers and university advice is where our Futures Department really comes into its own for Senior & Sixth Form Students, providing guidance and advice for higher education or the many career paths available.
Post 18 Pathways
We work with individual students to lead them through the application processes for their chosen post Sixth Form pathway, using the online platform Unifrog.
The Futures Department offers a bespoke service that is tailored to the unique educational and career needs of our students, recognising and playing to their strengths and interests.
Through a combined programme of PSHEE talks and assemblies, large careers fairs and visiting professionals, the Futures Team provides exceptional support, advice and guidance to ensure pupils have all the information they require to make an informed choice about their future.
The Department works closely with the Head of Sixth Form to nurture students through the process of their individual application.
College fairs, university visits and careers events
Whether students are interested in pursuing further education in the UK, Europe or the US, or keen to move into employment, we offer college fairs and university visits, open days and careers events, enabling them to make contacts with selected representatives who can give them tailored advice from their personal and professional experience.
For those students who are interested in apprenticeships, we have a number of links with alumni involved with Degree Apprenticeships, offering exceptional guidance across the rigorous application processes.
The Futures Department’s in-depth programme of enrichment talks in Prep School, Senior School and TSI ensures each student has every opportunity possible to explore the options available before deciding their future pathway.
Where are they now?
Our alumni go on to have successful careers in a variety of areas including medicine, law, finance, health, education, business management, sport, and the entertainment industry, to name but a few.
The sense of global reach at Taunton School continues long after students leave. Our alumni association is a global network of thousands of people, of all ages.
Book a Visit with us
Join our Head of Sixth Form Jennifer Taylor, and the Taunton School Leadership Team at an upcoming open event.
This is the best way for prospective families to experience Taunton School with the opportunity to meet members of staff, our current Sixth Form students, tour the state-of-the-art facilities and ask questions. Join our in-person open mornings or attend virtually. We run dedicated Sixth Form Open Evenings in the Autumn Term each year as well.

We believe in the transformative power of drama education
Our vibrant Drama Department is a hub of creativity, innovation, and expression, where students explore the rich tapestry of human experiences through the art of performance.
With the opportunity to be involved in our exciting stage productions either as actors, designers, directors, or assisting in a technical capacity such as costume, lighting design or sound, we ignite the imaginations of our students and empower them to become confident, collaborative, empathetic, and resilient individuals.
Whether you dream of treading the boards in a classic Shakespearean play or exploring contemporary issues through devised theatre, our diverse and extensive range of co-curricular activities cater to all interests and skill levels.
We offer four major productions each year
Alongside academic lessons, our highly experienced Drama teachers and full time Performing Arts Technical Manager produce a performance schedule that enjoys four major productions each year; past productions include ‘Romeo and Juliet’, ‘A Christmas Carol’, ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’, and ‘Brontë’, with regular whole school musicals such as ‘Les Misérables’ and, most recently, ‘Legally Blonde’ showcasing the breadth and depth of Performing Arts talent from within our school community.
There are many Drama clubs to be involved with too, such as ‘Musical Theatre’, ‘Technical Theatre’ and ‘Improv’, through to individual and group Speech and Drama lessons where students can work towards LAMDA qualifications.

We offer a supportive and inclusive community
Community is so important to us. We provide a supportive environment where students are encouraged to take risks, embrace failure as a learning opportunity, and celebrate others’ successes. This culminates in our Performing Arts Awards Evening at the end of the Summer term, where students from Music, Drama, Debating, and Dance come together to watch a few select performances and congratulate each other for their contributions throughout the year.
Diversity is celebrated and inclusion is non-negotiable. Our Drama Department is a welcoming space where students from all backgrounds come together to collaborate, learn, and grow as artists and individuals. From auditioning for and receiving places at Drama Schools or on specialist courses with world-renowned organisations, to participating in national competitions, our students gain invaluable real-world experience that prepares them for success on the stage.
Whether you are a seasoned performer or taking your first steps onto the stage, we offer a dynamic and enriching experience like no other. Come and discover the magic of drama education with us!

pageCache.pageTitle: Music at Taunton School | Find Your Exceptional
pageCache.text:
Music is central to life at Taunton School
Our aim is to provide enriching musical opportunities for everyone in the community, enabling every member of the school to develop their talents, and celebrating all genres of music.
Students at Taunton School regularly secure places at conservatories and top university Music departments. Year 12 and Year 13 students study A-Level and IB diploma Music courses, and numbers are strong at GCSE. Current students have gained representation in the National Children’s Choir, British Youth Music Theatre, and Somerset County Youth Orchestra, among many other ensembles. Recent alumni have gained places for the further study of music at the Royal College of Music, RNCM, Trinity Laban, Berklee College and at Durham University.
MUSICAL PATHWAYS
We are passionate about developing each student as a musician. These musical pathways are designed to allow musicians of all levels of experience to develop and thrive. We are able to offer personalised programmes of development, and musical opportunities are not limited to the those listed in each category.
HIGH PERFORMANCE
ASPIRING MUSICIANS
HIGH PERFORMANCE
For musicians who are ambitious to work at the highest levels of performance, we offer a personalised programme of study, and outstanding opportunities for solo and ensemble performance, including:
– Individual lessons with highly-respected specialist visiting music teachers
– Masterclasses with internationally recognised performers
– Concerto performance opportunities accompanied by professional orchestra
– Chamber music suited to the individual, with weekly coaching sessions
– Tailored individual rehearsal and coaching sessions with a dedicated accompanist
– Readily available practice facilities, including use of Steinway grand piano in the outstanding acoustic of the Gwyn Williams Room
– High-profile external performance opportunities and full support in entering local, regional and national festivals and competitions, exams such as diplomas, and preparing auditions for national level ensembles and for music colleges
– Musical leadership within a range of large ensembles performing inspiring repertoire
– Individual development sessions with a professional composer, for aspiring composers of all musical styles
– Weekly scholars’ programme focussed on areas such as mindset, practice, memorisation, improvisation, composition and conducting skills
ASPIRING MUSICIANS
For musicians who have some experience as performers and whose skills are progressing, we provide a full range of support, and we believe passionately that performance opportunities at the right levels can be key to the development of musical interest and skills. The programme of study includes:
– Individual lessons available on request with highly-respected specialist visiting music teachers
– A wealth of ensemble music-making opportunities, including four different choirs, an orchestra and string orchestra, musical theatre club, brass ensemble, percussion ensemble, dance band, funk band, rock band and many more small ensembles
– A range of individual performance opportunities, including Tea Time Concerts, performances in chapel, Evening Recitals, internal solo vocal and instrumental competitions with visiting adjudicators, and entry to classes at Taunton Festival of the Arts
– Tailored support for exams with all music exam boards (if exams are desired), including a dedicated accompanist and aural training sessions
– Distinctive opportunities for songwriters and pop/rock musicians, including band rehearsals, Taunton Sessions performances and the opportunity to record in the fully-equipped studio
– The opportunity to audition for lead roles or chorus involvement in full-scale musical theatre performances at professional venues
OPPORTUNITIES FOR ALL
Taunton School Music Department offers a broad range of musical opportunities, shown by the diversity of styles performed by the school’s large ensembles. We encourage every student to experience a musical event, as a performer or audience member. For those who are beginning to explore music for the first time, the opportunities include:
– Unauditioned membership of large musical ensembles led by specialist staff, with a focus on the joy of music-making
– Engagement with a huge range of musical styles, including classical, musical theatre, pop and film music.
– The experience of performing as a member of a large ensemble within full-scale concert performances, accompanied by professional musicians
– Individual lessons available on request with highly-respected specialist visiting music teachers
– Collaborations with the Drama department on fully inclusive musical productions
– Tea Time Concert performance opportunities, which include musicians performing a short piece for the first time
An extensive programme of ensembles and performances
The department boasts an extensive programme of ensembles and performances, meeting the musical interests and needs of our entire student body. Among the co-curricular groups rehearsing regularly in the department are Taunton School Chorus, the Chapel Choir, Advanced Vocal Ensemble, the Community Choir, Symphony Orchestra, String Orchestra, Wind Band, Dance Band, Funk Band, Brass Ensemble, Percussion Ensemble, several Rock Bands, and a rapidly growing provision for Chamber Music.
The annual calendar of music events features over 100 performances, including a Concerto Competition, large-scale termly concerts, a Choral Concert, Advent and Christmas Carol Services, full-scale Musical Productions, tours in the UK and overseas, Pro Corda Festival Competition, Evening Recitals, regular Teatime Concerts, Evensongs and other services, Masterclasses and concert trips, Contemporary Music Evenings, and much much more.
Our most recent musical production was Legally Blonde, performed by a cast of 70, seen by over 1500 people in 5 sell-out performances at Somerset’s leading performing arts venue at The Brewhouse in Taunton.
Recent masterclass and workshop leaders have included Daniel Pailthorpe (co-principal flute of the BBC Symphony Orchestra), Dr Jonathan James (animateur with the London Symphony Orchestra and Bournemouth Symphony Orchestra), and Clive Hughes (violinist, formerly of the Smith Quartet).

Play Addams Family

Play Magic of the Musicals
A wealth of opportunity and excellent facilities
Under the leadership of the Director of Music, there is an Assistant Director of Music, a full time Music Teacher (Deputy Head), the Coordinator of Instrumental Studies, a full-time Head of Keyboard, a School Organist, a Graduate Resident Assistant in Music, and a vibrant group of outstanding Visiting Music Teachers, many of whom take leadership roles in co-curricular ensembles.
The Music School has its own building, situated next to the school’s historic Chapel, which seats 300 and is used extensively for services and many high-profile concerts. Other performance spaces include the Gwyn Williams Recital Room, seating up to 80, and the Old Library, seating 140. There are three grand pianos, together with high-quality Yamaha uprights in each of the teaching rooms, and a Nord Stage 4 digital stage piano.
The Music Technology Room has 12 iMacs, each equipped with Sibelius and Logic software, there is a separate Sixth Form teaching room, and a fully equipped Recording Studio. Instrumental teaching and practice facilities include a specialist percussion room, chamber music room and a keyboard room with two pianos, alongside numerous teaching/practice rooms.
Visit Us

More Than 60 Co-curricular Clubs
We are committed to educating the whole child, which is critical to enabling pupils to ‘find their exceptional’.
We offer more than 60 Co-curricular clubs, with 15 different instruments available to learn and 12 competitive sports at national level.
Almost half of our children are involved in the School Choirs; over 150 pupils participate in major music concerts; and more than 70 pupils participate in Taunton Drama Festival each year.
We are ambitious
Developing the whole child is vital to us. The Prep School has an exhaustive and wide range of co-curricular clubs which enable all children to ‘find their exceptional’. This enables all children to understand the ’Taunton 12’, personal characteristic which will enable them to thrive and to be successful.
Celebrating diversity, we ensure every pupil can engage regardless of background or abilities, believing that a rich tapestry of talents contributes to a vibrant, and dynamic school community.
Ambition is a fundamental pillar of our co-curricular philosophy, inspiring our pupils to set ambitious goals and pursue their dreams with determination. Whether in academics, sports, or performing arts, our activities ignite a sense of ambition, propelling pupils toward their aspirations and preparing them for futures where they can leave a meaningful and lasting impact.
We are a creative school nurturing talent
All pupils enjoy curriculum based lessons in Drama and Music but for so many pupils, the performing arts is a key area where they ‘find their exceptional’ through an exhaustive number of clubs, concerts and competitions.
In the 2023 Taunton Drama Festival, 71 TPS pupils took part in 117 different performances at the competition. From these children, 45 pupils in Year’s 2 to Year 8 were awarded with ‘First, Second and Third Placing’s’ in various classes.
In Summer 2023, 59 TPS pupils, in year-groups ranging from Year 2 to Year 8 took Vanguard Speech & Drama exams. The average mark of our exam results was 90% and 18 children were awarded with a mark in the ‘Honours’ banding (a mark of 90% or greater).
We excel at sport
We offer a range of sports with more than 800 fixtures a year for our main sports.

At Taunton Prep School, our outstanding facilities and expert staff provide pupils with a broad and enriching educational experience in Sport, Art, Design Technology, Music, Drama, Dance, and over 60 other co-curricular activities.

Welcome from Nursery Admissions Officer Alison Salvador
“Having been a pupil at Taunton School myself and watched my own three sons thrive here I feel I am perfectly placed to help guide and support parents through the difficult decision of choosing a school. Early Years Education is such a vitally important step in a child’s development and education, and Taunton School Nursery is an incredibly special place. Entry to our Nursery
Admission to Taunton School Nursery is available for children aged between 6 months and 4 years.
We have 4 Nursery classes grouped by age and the children move up to the next room each academic year. From Nursery the next step is a seamless transition into the Reception Class of our Pre-Prep School.
Early Years Entitlement
We have agreed to adopt and work in Partnership with the Somerset Code of Practice for Early Years.
The county of Somerset offers a maximum of 570 hours per year of Early Years Entitlement (EYE) for eligible families of children aged 9months to 5 years. There are a further 570 hours available for qualifying families.
There is no minimum entitlement per day but the maximum hours per week that may be claimed is 15 or, for those families qualifying for the additional entitlement, the maximum amount of hours which can be claimed each week is 30.
Early Years Entitlement is free at the point of delivery and covers the delivery of the Early Years curriculum. It is important to note that this funding does not cover meals and snacks or the use of our purpose-built facilities, swimming teachers, specialist music staff, language teachers, dance lessons, PE lessons and other specialist activities. These additional facilities, lessons and activities form part of our Taunton School Nursery Exceptional package which is subject to additional voluntary charges to access.
Somerset County Council provides lots of information and guidance to help you make an informed choice. More information is available online on www.somersetchoices.org.uk or by calling 0300 1232224.
Please contact our Nursery Admissions Administrator on 01823 703302 or tppsadmissions@tauntonschool.co.uk for further information.
Nursery Admissions Process
Here’s our easy step by step guide to the Nursery admissions process.
Please fill out the enquiry form to express your interest, or telephone 01823 703339 with your child’s name and date of birth/due date.
Following your enquiry, we invite you for a bespoke visit of Taunton School Nursery so you can experience our wonderful setting for yourself.
We also run Nursery & Pre-Prep Information Events, which you can easily book online.
To apply for a place at Nursery, you need to complete the registration form, pay the non-refundable registration fee and provide a copy of your child’s birth certificate or passport.
We encourage you to visit the nursery prior to registering, but if this is not possible, we can answer any questions over the phone or email.
Any child may be registered from birth, and we are happy to accept registration forms prior to the birth of your child, if you are comfortable with this.
Nursery places are subject to availability. If a place is not available, parents will be given the opportunity to join the waiting list and will not be charged a registration fee. When a place becomes available within the relevant Nursery Room, the parents of the child at the top of the waiting list will be contacted and offered a place. The registration fee will then need to be paid.
Offers are made on a first come first served basis, although siblings of current Taunton School pupils are given priority.
We will send an offer letter to you, specifying the sessions that are booked and the start date. If you wish to accept the place, you will need to complete and sign the Acceptance Forms and return them to Nursery Admissions with the acceptance deposit*. You will be requested to respond within a specified time if you wish to accept the offer made, otherwise the offer will lapse.
Additional sessions may be requested once your child has joined the Nursery, space permitting. Should you wish to decrease your days or withdraw your child from Nursery, we ask for one term’s notice in writing, which must be acknowledged by Nursery Admissions.
*The Acceptance Deposit is refundable for children who progress through to the Preparatory School Year 3.
As your start date approaches, we will invite you to attend an induction meeting with your child’s new Nursery Room Leader. We will also send you an information booklet (‘All About Me’) for you to complete and bring with you to this meeting. This book asks for information about your family and your child. All this information will help us to get to know you and your child quickly and helps with the settling-in process.
The induction meeting is a time to ask more questions (no matter how small!), review your information booklet together and discuss how you may like to manage the initial settling-in process of your child. Some children and parents prefer a short, quick drop-off, whilst others need a gradual settling-in programme.
If you are joining the Nursery in September, we also have a new pupils and parents tea party in our grounds the day before Autumn Term commences. There is always a lovely atmosphere at the tea party. It gives your family and your child an opportunity to meet our Nursery team, explore the site and familiarise the children with new environments.

Our History
Taunton School was founded in 1847 and has a rich 175-year history. Originally housed in what has now become one of the boys’ boarding houses, Fairwater, the school moved to its current location in 1870. The now Grade II listed gothic-style building was constructed by Joseph James, complete with an impressive tower.
In 1907, William Henry Wills, 1st Baron Winterstoke, sponsored the construction of the Chapel, which to this day still plays a key role in the school’s community.
In 1973 Taunton School became one of the first co-educational independent schools by welcoming both boys and girls.
In 1996, Taunton School was one of the first schools to open an International Study Centre, which became known as Taunton School International (TSI) in 2010. TSI now offers a one-year and two-year GCSE/Pre-IB Programme as well as a one-year or two-year Business Foundation Programme.
In 2007, as well as offering A-Levels, Taunton School became an IB World School and more recently, has also added BTECs in Business and Sport and Exercise Science.
In 2012, Taunton School opened its International Middle School in the nearby village of Kingston-St-Mary, providing an ideal stepping stone for international students into mainstream British independent schools.
In 2020, Taunton School invested £4 million in the construction of a state-of-the-art dining hall, located in the heart of the school, providing students with exceptional dining experience, with all meals cooked by our own chefs on site.

Debating and Public Speaking has a long history at Taunton School
The Debating and Public Speaking Society is a popular and thriving club and has had a long history at Taunton School. There are regular formal debates, an event referred to as the Burke Debate, and there are also opportunities for students to engage in less formal debating sessions to hone their skills.
We also enjoy success in external Debating and Public Speaking Competitions, being regular participants in the English Speaking Union’s Schools’ Mace, the ESU’s Churchill Public Speaking Competition, the ESU’s Performing Shakespeare Competition, and the Oxford Union School Debating Competition.
We are a founding member of the World Individual Debating and Public Speaking Championship
We also enjoy success in external Debating and Public Speaking Competitions, being regular participants in the English Speaking Union’s Schools’ Mace, the ESU’s Churchill Public Speaking Competition, the ESU’s Performing Shakespeare Competition, and the Oxford Union School Debating Competition.
We are also a founding member of the World Individual Debating and Public Speaking Championships; this is an international debating competition, in which we send students to compete at an international debating level.
Cultivating a mindset for life and a freedom to be yourself
The Debating and Public Speaking Society at Taunton School aims to equip students with the necessary skills and knowledge to become effective speakers and debaters. The society is open to individuals of all ages in the Senior School.
Students participating in the Debating and Public Speaking Society develop their communication skills, including verbal and nonverbal communication, active listening, and critical thinking. There are plenty of opportunities to engage in constructive debate and dialogue, in both formal and informal settings, allowing students to develop a deeper understanding of complex issues and diverse perspectives.
Students learn to enhance their ability to express themselves clearly and persuasively in a variety of settings, including public speaking engagements, but also in all other aspects of their present and future lives. This is all with the intention of build students’ confidence and self-esteem; enabling them to take on leadership roles and pursue their goals with greater enthusiasm and determination.
Model United Nations
The Model United Nations (MUN) Club at is a co-curricular activity that provides students with an opportunity to participate in simulations of the United Nations. The MUN Club meets regularly, and members engage in activities that prepare them for MUN conferences.
The club is overseen by a staff member, but student leaders (called Secretary Generals) organise the meetings, coordinate activities, and guide members in the development of their skills. The club is open to the whole student body of the Secondary School, but usually attracts students who are interested in international relations, diplomacy, public speaking, and critical thinking.
In the meetings, members participate in debates, practise their public speaking skills, learn about global issues, and hone their negotiation and diplomacy skills. They may also engage in research, writing, and presenting on specific issues or countries.
The MUN Club attends local and regional conferences, where they have the opportunity to participate in United Nations simulations with other schools. At these conferences, students represent a specific country and work with other delegates to draft resolutions, negotiate with other delegations, and ultimately pass resolutions on a specific issue.
The MUN Club provides a unique opportunity for students to develop skills, gain knowledge about global issues, and build relationships with like-minded peers. It can also be a valuable addition to University applications and a stepping stone towards future leadership roles in international affairs.

A day in the life of Taunton prep school
Crafting harmony, our school day blends academic rigor, co-curricular exploration, and personal growth, providing a structured yet dynamic environment to cater to diverse student needs and interests.
Registration 8.20am marks the beginning of the school day with an initial touch base with Form tutors and then community time. This is an opportunity for us to come together as a whole, share key messages and celebrate pupils’ success. These activities involve assemblies, chapel, extended tutor time and a dedicated whole school reading session. Our chapel is led by our own reverend Getman who tailors the service to various current topics such as world events, and religious milestones throughout the year.
Our lessons are 1 hour in length and the morning session is broken by a break at 11am for 25 minutes. This is an opportunity for the pupils have a snack and let off some steam on the playground, MUGA pitch and in the warmer months, our school field before heading back to lessons.
Lunchtime is an hour long and starts at 12.30pm. During this time, pupils take lunch in our modern purpose-built dining room, they have time outside with their friends and there are also a variety of co-curricular activities that take place which are optional.
The afternoon begins with lessons which run through the afternoon to 3.50pm and a final touch base with their tutor.
Pupils can enjoy a quick snack and playtime break from 4:00pm – 4:15pm, then after school activities begin at 4:15pm-5:15pm. Prep is from 4:30pm–5:15pm and pupils may stay for an extended prep session from 5:15pm–5:45pm. Buses depart at 5:30pm marking the end of the day.

We aim to ensure every student feels valued through engagement with Sport
Taunton School Sport begins with an ‘End in Mind’ approach and is driven to support the whole community in developing a lifelong enjoyment of sport and exercise. The department aims to ensure that every student feels valued through engagement with Sport, fostering an inclusive climate that ensures participation and competition work in harmony to deliver outstanding outcomes, whilst developing good people who will make positive contributions to the world.
Our sporting ethos is built on the concept of ‘GRIT’
The sporting ethos of the school is built on the concept of ‘GRIT’, encouraging students to embrace an understanding that perseverance and passion will lead to achievement of ambitious long-term goals. The four main areas of ‘GRIT’ – Grounded, Resilient, Integrity and Tenacity – are explored extensively throughout the school year, in both individual and team sports. Our students are actively encouraged to transfer their core skills, competencies, behaviours and attitudes far beyond the sporting arena, impacting positively all areas of school life.
A wealth of sporting opportunity
We support and create opportunities for all students to contribute to the sporting story of Taunton School, whether selected to represent a school team or through participation in a house competition. There are over 120 representative teams across 20 different sports, demonstrating the breadth of offer at Taunton School.
Our extensive programme also enjoys outstanding levels of achievement, with considerable success in county, regional and national competitions. Many of our students perform at age grade county, regional, and international levels across a range of sports, with many choosing to continue with high performance sport at university, often receiving scholarships to support their studies.
The Three Sport Pathways
Taunton School focuses on a multi-disciplinary approach to school sport, with each student encouraged to be an active participant in the core sport of that term. We believe the later a student specialises in training and performance, the greater chance that student has for holistic, physical, mental and social development.
We have three sporting pathways, designed carefully to enhance and develop all levels of ability, experience, and ambition. Each and every student at the school is able to access one of these pathways, central to our fully inclusive offering:

Potential High-Performance Pathway (PHPP)
Not all young people fit neatly into year groups where they all develop at the same rate physically, mentally, and socially. Development can happen at different times to different people, dependent on birth month, previous access to sport coaching and competition, and genetic dependent maturation. With these issues in mind, we have created the ‘Potential High Performer Pathway’.
Potential High Performers are students in Year 9 and 10 who have aspirations to achieve excellence in the Senior Upper School and beyond. These sessions are focused on students who demonstrate good ability, high levels of coachability, and are motivated to improve in a chosen pathway.
Performance Development Pathway (PDP)
For students new to the school or those who are simply enjoying their first experience of hockey, cricket, tennis, netball, or rugby, their journey and development starts from the first time they walk on the astro, pitch, or court.
The Performance Development Pathway will sit at the beginning of their journey, encouraging participation, with ability or experience removed as a barrier.
Using a coaching syllabus developed by each Head of Sport, the pathway will include specialist coaching before students are given the opportunity to engage competitively within our in-house games programmes and fixtures against other schools within our regular Saturday block opponents. We hope to provide a pathway of opportunity, bridging the gap between experience levels, access to high level coaching, a chance to move up to higher representational teams, but mostly to feel valued and developed.
Taunton School’s Sport Impact Report
It is with great pride that we can share with you the many successes and highlights from the past academic year at Taunton School in this report. It is designed to recognise, celebrate, and highlight individual and collective achievements of the Taunton School Sport community.
Sports Facilities
Taunton School provides extensive, state-of-the-art sporting facilities across our 56-acre campus.
There are exceptional indoor and outdoor facilities for traditional team games and other sports, including three indoor sports venues, two indoor swimming pools, an indoor golf simulator, a well-equipped fitness suite, eight netball courts, three multi-purpose floodlit Astro Turf pitches, a purpose-built dance studio, an athletics area, 4 flood-lit hard tennis courts, two squash courts and a climbing wall, as well as our grass pitches for Cricket, Rugby and Football.
Athletic Development
We are committed to providing quality support for all students who have a goal to maximise their potential and wellbeing.
A weekly programme is delivered each term that all students can access, be that within the core games programme, within individual support sessions, or in our extensive club’s programme, taking place before school, during lunchtime or after school. The programme focuses on ‘Long Term Athletic Development’ through improvement of students’ physical ability, movement literacy and robustness, embedded within our multi-sport pathway.
Student programmes are planned and monitored to ensure each student receives the necessary support to achieve their personal best. Liaison with external agencies for students on pathway sport gives a holistic view of the student’s lifestyle and wellbeing.

Rugby
The Rugby programme operates throughout the academic year and is led by a dedicated Director of Rugby and Assistant Director of Rugby. We field at least two teams per age group and maintain a full and competitive fixture list against leading schools across the South West and nationally. Our teams also compete in the U14, U15, U16 and U18 National Schools competitions.
In the Spring term, focus shifts to Rugby 7s. The School proudly hosts the West of England 7s tournament, before all age groups — boys and girls — compete in the world-renowned Rosslyn Park National Schools Sevens.
An extensive pre-season programme runs during the Summer term and throughout August, ensuring players are fully prepared for a demanding and ambitious fixture schedule.
We are supported by an outstanding team of coaches who are driven to ensure that every student shares their passion for the game. Rugby is a sport built on control, trust, loyalty and humility, and we expect all players to demonstrate these qualities both on and off the field.
We are extremely proud to be partnered with Bristol Bears, one of the leading professional clubs in English rugby. This is a genuine and embedded partnership, with a number of coaching and performance staff working across both the school and Bristol Bears programmes. This close collaboration ensures alignment in coaching philosophy, player development, strength and conditioning, and performance analysis.
As our affiliated academy club, Bristol Bears provide a clear development pathway for aspiring players. Students benefit from performance profiling, specialist expertise and exposure to professional standards of preparation and review. We also maintain strong links with local clubs including Taunton RFC, North Petherton RFC and Wiveliscombe RFC, ensuring that players at all stages of development have access to competitive and supportive rugby environments.
Hockey
Hockey
The Hockey programme operates throughout all three terms and has a dedicated Director of Hockey who is an FIH Level 3 qualified coach and Great Britain Advanced Coach Programme, along with an Assistant Director of Hockey and a team of qualified and experienced coaches. We offer opportunities to play England Hockey Tier 1 competitions in both indoor and outdoor hockey, including weekly fixtures against other schools, with four Senior Teams and Junior A, B, and C teams regularly representing the school.
We offer a specialised goalkeeper club that enables all student goalkeepers to receive technical sessions, whilst offering small group and open-pitch sessions for all students to access and use the astros independently when they have free time. Students can also book into specific small group sessions where they can work directly with coaches to improve technical proficiency and game play. This is complemented by our in-depth video analysis of both training sessions and matches, further aiding student development.
In September 2024 the School opened two new state-of-the-art floodlit AstroTurf pitches. The programme has strong links with Taunton Vale Hockey Club, ISCA and Ashmoor Hockey Club, and are fully supportive of a large number of players who engage in the England Hockey Junior Pathways with numerous students in County Hockey and Talent Academy. We offer performance profiling to help individuals identify strengths and weaknesses and take ownership of their development.

The provision is extensive and inclusive, offering opportunities for players of all abilities to develop and thrive — whether at a recreational level or within a high-performance pathway. We field six senior teams, alongside Junior A, B, C, D and E teams, all of which compete in a strong fixture programme against leading schools across the South West.
The School competes in the National Schools’ competitions annually, with teams consistently achieving success at County, Regional and National levels. This sustained success reflects both the quality of coaching and the ambition embedded within the programme.
Player development sits at the heart of our provision. Students can access weekly small-group technical sessions to refine specific areas of their game, as well as specialist shooting and defensive clinics designed to enhance positional expertise. This tailored approach ensures that every athlete is appropriately challenged and supported.
Our Year 9 cohort participates in the prestigious International Netball Festival in Paris each October, and students across the programme are offered opportunities to tour internationally, gaining invaluable competitive and cultural experiences.
We are proud to have numerous athletes representing at U13 and U15 County Academy level, within Franchise Academy Development Centres (ADC), Player Development Programmes (PDP), National Performance League (NPL) squads, Senior Regional League and National level netball. Academic Excellence Taunton Prep School
We Aim High & Try Our Best
At Taunton Prep School pupils are taught by subject specialists in classrooms with a high level of technical equipment including our own Science and Design and Technology labs. We prioritise positive behaviour, respect, and active engagement in lessons. Our students consistently exceed national averages in Maths and English, showcasing our commitment to unlocking academic potential for all. Our scholarship programme, spanning from Year 5 to Year 13, fosters academic and personal growth. Mentored by dedicated staff, scholars thrive in diverse learning environments, embracing challenges and opportunities for excellence.
We challenge students to excel through community projects, national competitions, and enrichment sessions. In Years 7 & 8, students participate in weekly enrichment sessions, exploring diverse perspectives and leadership opportunities within the school. Our academic community celebrates both outstanding achievements and individual progress, recognising and supporting students on their journey to excellence and personal growth.
Uncovering Potential & Inspiring Learning
We Are Active Learners & Curious
At Taunton Prep School, we nurture every child’s potential. In Years 3 to 5, our ‘book-based’ creative curriculum approach integrates English, History, Geography, and creative subjects through captivating topics. Students explore diverse texts, go on trips, and engage with guest speakers.
Specialists in DT, Art, Performing Arts, and French provide continuity from Year 3 to Year 6. In Years 6 to 8, students broaden their options, including languages taught by Senior School staff, preparing them for a seamless transition.
We pride ourselves by ensuring that all year groups and pupils have a broad and balanced curriculum which includes Drama, Music, Art and Design Technology alongside the core of Maths, English, Science, History, Philosophy and Geography.
We Try New Things & Embrace Challenges
As an all-through school, we benefit from excellent teaching facilities across all areas of the curriculum offering a wealth of opportunity.
We recognise that learning is achieved through a variety of mediums and are delighted each year to welcome authors, poets, artists, philosophers and scientists, providing opportunities for pupils to try new things.As part of our timetabled lessons for younger pupils we provide musical instrument taster sessions and their first experience of a choir.
We integrate elements such as STEM days, PSHEE workshops and outdoor education as pupils move up the school as part of our school experience. At TPS, we want pupils to be curious and independent thinkers, developing a love of learning and a desire to be an active member of our school community.
We Celebrate Diversity & Support Every Student
At Taunton Prep School, we are proud of our inclusive international community, fostering respect and tolerance among our students. For those with English as a Second Language (EAL), we offer personalised support through additional lessons taught by specialist staff, tailored to their individual needs.
Understanding that each student is unique, our dedicated SEND department provides highly qualified specialist teachers who offer one-to-one tuition in Maths and English. We believe in promoting confidence and independence within a nurturing environment, enabling students to take ownership of their learning journey.

pageCache.text:
Prioritising wellbeing & pastoral care
We prioritise excellent pastoral care as a collective effort between staff, students, and parents, fostering open communication and empathy.
Pupils are encouraged to express themselves with humility, engagement and kindness, all the while benefitting from the nurturing care provided through individualised support.
Developing a mindset for life
We have high expectations of our pupils in terms of behaviour, equipping them with the tools to develop a mindset for life as confident, global citizens with self-discipline and a growing sense of responsibility towards themselves and others. They are able to converse with their peers and others with interest, good manners and confidence.
All pupils are placed into one of our four Houses for the whole of their time in the Prep School and a vibrant programme of competitions and fun activities creates a sense of belonging, pride and good-natured rivalry.
In Year 9, our students transition to Senior School, prepared for new challenges. Year 8 marks a pivotal stage where students assume leadership roles, contributing to our vibrant community through initiatives like Sports, Digital, Chapel, and Junior Leaders, fostering collaboration and maturity.
Comprehensive Wellbeing Support at Taunton Prep School
In addition to our student Playground Ambassadors, Leaders, and Champions, Mrs Day collaborates closely with tutors and pastoral heads of year to help support all the children. We also have access to health centre staff including mental health nurses, counsellors and Merlin and Ralph, our school therapy dogs.
Pastoral Care Structure
The form teacher plays a central role in our pastoral system, providing daily guidance and support to their classes, overseeing both academic and pastoral aspects.
Four Pastoral Heads of Year offer additional care, support, and discipline, overseen by the Deputy Head Pastoral, Senior Headmaster, and ultimately, the Head. Fostering a sense of belonging and respect helps children thrive and be themselves.
We are again and again overwhelmed by this passion to nurture and to encourage- by the warmth of the whole team. This is outstanding!
Testimonial
A School for Pupils of All Faiths and None
Spirituality and understanding major world religions are integral to our students’ personal growth. While rooted in Christian principles, our open community embraces children of all faiths and backgrounds. Our vibrant Chapel, led by the Chaplain, fosters worship and peace.
Partnerships with Parents
Effective education depends upon the strength of the triangle that exists between the pupil, the parents and the school. When all three points of that triangle are pulling in the same direction, there is no limit to what can be achieved. Our philosophy is simple – we succeed together.
Our parents can always arrange face to face contact with any member of staff. Telephone conversations can always be arranged, or parents may choose to communicate via email.
